subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should Browser upload gain an explicit drop/paste/native-drag file-injection mode for custom uploaders, and what operator-visible security contract should that mode use?
rationale: The implementation would intentionally pass managed local file contents through page-controlled event handlers outside the standard file-input boundary, so automation should not choose the security semantics by inference.

options.title: Add explicit custom-uploader mode
options.body: Create a named Browser upload mode such as drop-file or paste-file with managed-path validation, docs, tests, and live proof; leave ordinary upload behavior unchanged.

options.title: Keep file-input upload only
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to synthesize arbitrary page drop, paste, or drag file delivery.

options.title: Allow silent fallback
options.body: Permit upload to infer a drop/paste/native-drag fallback after file-input upload fails, accepting higher surprise and security-review burden.

recommendation.title: Add explicit custom-uploader mode
recommendation.body: Create a named Browser upload mode such as drop-file or paste-file with managed-path validation, docs, tests, and live proof; leave ordinary upload behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Browser upload feature history and the current helper family trace most strongly through steipete’s commits.
